sections.overview: Philodromus margaritatus is a Palearctic spider in the family Philodromidae.
sections.identification: Its flattened body is about 5–7 mm long, with variable contrasting markings and spiny, banded legs.
sections.habitat: It lives on tree bark and foliage, especially on lichen-covered trunks, and is recorded more rarely on rocks.
sections.diet: It ambushes mainly flies while concealed against lichen on tree trunks.
sections.behavior: Adults are observed from May to August in the French Alps; its camouflage makes it easy to overlook.
sections.reproduction: The female guards an egg sac woven against tree bark during incubation.
sections.ecology: It can be confused with Philodromus emarginatus; close examination, including genital structures, may be needed for identification.
sections.conservation: Regional assessments differ: British sources report Near Threatened, while the German Red List records Least Concern; these categories apply to their respective regions.
